description:
Goal
Run a structured game day for Dedicated Burst Capacity before GA readiness gates. Validate that guardrails protect non-burst tenants, that SLO-based gates work, and that on-call has a clear, repeatable mitigation path.

Scope
- Execute scenarios from the game day plan (synthetic bursts + induced failures).
- Capture observations, timelines, and concrete outcomes (what worked / what didn’t).
- Produce follow-up fixes as Linear tickets (with owners) and ensure they are tied to GA checklist.

References
- Confluence: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/burst-capacity-game-day-plan.json
- Runbook draft: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/burst-pool-overload-mitigation-runbook.json
- Dashboards catalog: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/burst-capacity-dashboards.json
- SLOs/alerts: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-burst-slos-and-alerting.json

Planned participants
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (facilitator), Sean Gallagher (SLO gate sign-off)
- Platform: Ethan Park, Jordan Lee (policy/determinism), Vikram Singh (data plane)
- Routing: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Infra/Fleet: Keiko Yamamoto (guardrails), Vanessa Ortiz (pool capacity)
- Observability: Allison Grant / Sergio Costa

Environment
- Staging for initial dry run; then canary prod slice (internal workloads only) with feature flags.
- Burst enabled for 2 internal tenants + 1 dedicated test tenant (non-customer), across us-east/H100.

Scenario list (executed)
1) Pool saturation under coordinated burst
- Drive burst traffic to exceed shared pool headroom while keeping baseline dedicated steady.
- Validate: admissions deny w/ correct reason; queue/backpressure behavior matches ADR; circuit breaker does not trip prematurely.

2) Telemetry lag / staleness
- Introduce 60–120s lag in pool saturation signals (simulate metrics pipeline delay).
- Validate: determinism guarantees; no oscillatory admit/deny; fairness not starved due to stale utilization.

3) Admission controller partial outage / elevated latency
- Inject 5xx + 500ms–2s latency on admission controller.
- Validate: routing fallback behavior, timeouts, and that we fail closed vs fail open per policy; verify user-facing errors are consistent.

4) Routing policy mismatch / config propagation delay
- Change tenant burst config mid-test (caps + cooldown) and observe propagation.
- Validate: audit event emitted, control plane reflects change, Console surfaces eventual consistency expectations.

5) Neighbor impact check (non-burst tenant)
- While burst tenant spikes, run steady load on a non-burst tenant.
- Validate: non-burst p95 and tail amplification within protected thresholds; SLO gate triggers if regression crosses threshold.

6) Global safety cap / emergency kill switch
- Force conditions to approach fleet safety cap.
- Validate: global breaker transitions and clear alerting; rollback steps are fast, safe, and verifiable.

Deliverables
- Game day notes + timeline + metrics screenshots (linked in comments).
- Final outcome summary + GA readiness recommendation.
- Follow-up tickets for any gaps.

Notes on expectations
- We are explicitly optimizing for non-burst protection: it’s OK for burst requests to be denied aggressively during safety events.
- Primary success criteria is predictable behavior + clear operator action paths, not maximizing burst admission rate.
acceptance_criteria: All planned scenarios executed in staging; at least scenarios (1), (3), and (6) executed in prod canary/internal workloads with feature flags
For each scenario: documented expected behavior vs observed behavior, including denial reason codes and any surprising client-facing responses
Confirmed alerts fire with acceptable noise: burst saturation, denial spikes, telemetry lag, admission controller errors, non-burst latency regression gate
Runbook validated end-to-end: operator can reduce caps, toggle per-tenant/region allow-list, and activate emergency kill switch within 10 minutes
Follow-up issues created for gaps, assigned to owners, and linked to GA checklist
outcome_summary: Executed game day on 2025-05-15 (staging dry run) and 2025-05-16 (prod canary, internal workloads only). Core guardrails behaved as designed under saturation and kill-switch conditions. Two notable gaps were found: (a) admission controller latency induced ambiguous client-side behavior due to missing explicit timeout budget + retry guidance in routing; (b) telemetry lag scenario caused short windows of unfair denials for a low-priority tenant (not starvation, but measurable deviation from expected fairness). SLO regression gate fired correctly when we intentionally pushed non-burst tail latency, but the alert annotation lacked direct runbook link and the rollback verification checklist was incomplete. GA recommendation: proceed with staged rollout only after follow-ups are implemented (timeout/retry policy, telemetry-lag hardening, runbook + docs polish).

comments: 2025-04-11 (Rafael Mendes): Drafted scenario list based on game day plan. Requesting Routing + Platform to confirm expected client-facing behavior when admission controller times out (fail-closed vs fail-open).

2025-04-18 (Allison Grant): Please ensure we test label/cardinality constraints under denial spikes; we saw staging cardinality blowups in other features when reason_code labels were unbounded. For this drill, keep the reason codes to the canonical set and verify dashboards don’t explode.

2025-04-23 (Keiko Yamamoto): For saturation scenario, don’t try to hit true fleet safety cap in prod. Use staging to force breaker behavior; in prod canary, validate toggle path + alerting without pushing neighbor SLOs beyond guardrail.

2025-05-06 (Jordan Lee): Determinism requirement reminder: admission decisions must be stable for a given request key within the retry window even if telemetry jitters. If we see oscillation under induced lag, treat as correctness bug (not just tuning).

2025-05-15 (Rafael Mendes): Staging dry run complete. Found: admission controller 500s propagate as mixed 503/429 at the gateway depending on path; hard to explain and not aligned to support guidance. Action: capture logs + open follow-up for routing error mapping + explicit timeout budget.

2025-05-16 (Sean Gallagher): Prod canary run: SLO regression gate fired as expected when we intentionally pushed non-burst p95. However the alert annotation doesn’t include the exact rollback commands / toggles. Please add runbook link + verification checklist before GA sign-off.

2025-05-20 (Sergio Costa): Dashboard review: denial reason breakdown is good; telemetry lag panel exists but threshold annotation unclear. Recommend adding ‘expected lag’ band and a note about the smoothing window so on-call knows when it’s benign vs dangerous.
2025-05-22 (Rafael Mendes): Follow-up tickets created and assigned. Marking ENG-4862 Done; GA readiness depends on follow-up completion + a short re-test of scenarios (3) and (2) in staging.
